recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Any future desire for a modern BPPC-specific IG or formal profile should be handled as a new scoped work-group effort, not as a current-core correction for FHIR-6285.
issue_request: FHIR-6285 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core CBCC change request asking for a Basic-ConsentDirective that could represent blanket BPPC/HIE policies including opt-in, opt-out, emergency or break-glass access, and summary-only sharing. The Jira resolution and comments say this was already applied and supported by examples.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly tagged FHIR-6285 was found. History shows the old Contract-based ConsentDirective profile/IG work existed around the request, Consent was later prototyped as a resource with examples and narrative in acc3f3137b, and the old Contract-based profile was restored in d313082ccd but is not the active current build mechanism.
additional_context: The current build uses Consent as an active resource. The old PCD IG entry is commented out, source/contract/consentdirective.profile.xml is not in the active [profiles] list, and source/fhir.ini notes that ConsentDirective became Consent. Current Consent narrative and definitions cover sourceAttachment/sourceReference, policyBasis, provision-based exceptions, opt-in/out patterns, and examples including Consent-In, Consent-Out, Consent-Emergency, and Consent-No-Emergency. A 2016 FMG Zulip thread mentioning GF#6285 supports interpreting the old profile request through the Consent resource transition.
reconciliation: No source change was made because adding or reviving a Basic-ConsentDirective profile would duplicate or regress the current Consent resource design. The active source already conveys the necessary BPPC stepping-stone support.

related_jiras.note: Raised related old Consent/ConsentDirective scope and 80-percent concerns and appears in the same profile-to-resource evidence path; not decided because it is broader than the seed's Basic-ConsentDirective BPPC examples.
Later Consent.category value set work on the active Consent resource; useful context but not the same source correction as FHIR-6285.
